It rolls back with the NPV P90 of 185, the low case, as a conservative fallback, which flips the EKPAN tree to Farm out.
It refuses with "Distribution payoff has no finite mean" and does not estimate one.
explanation: The engine will not guess a mean from percentiles, since the rollback needs the expectation and three percentiles do not fix it; on the EKPAN tree reading 390.0000 would have printed 94.5000.

prompt: In the Decision Tree Builder a user unlinks the Monte Carlo run from the EKPAN tree's success terminal. What does the terminal hold afterwards?
options: No payoff, which the engine reads as 0.0000, so the drill branch collapses and Farm out becomes the recommended first move.
The copied mean, 420.0000, as a fixed payoff, so the tree still rolls back to 105.0000.
The copied NPV P90 of 185.0000, since unlinking keeps the conservative copy of the run and discards the other two statistics.
The run's current mean, re-read once at the moment of unlinking, so the fixed payoff is up to date with any revaluation.
explanation: Linking stores a copy of the run's NPV mean, P90 and P10 at the moment of linking; nothing re-reads the run, and unlinking keeps the mean as a fixed payoff.

prompt: Every section of a Decision Studio brief carries a provenance line. What does the decision section's line establish about an EKPAN tree briefed at 105.0000?
options: That the tree's payoffs were discounted, since the provenance line records the rate the rollback applied at brief time.
That every cost box held a typed value, since a cleared cost is refused before a tree can be saved for a brief.
Which saved tree was rolled back, and nothing about whether its probabilities, payoffs or cost boxes are right.
That the tree agrees with the economics section, since both sections are stamped when the brief is built.
explanation: The rollback applies no discounting and a cleared cost box is silently 0; the EKPAN tree's drill branch worth 105.0000 still loses money with probability 0.500000, and the source is where checking starts.

prompt: A brief's economics section comes from an EPE Monte Carlo run revalued after it was linked into a tree, and its decision section re-rolls that tree at brief time. What can the page show?
options: A consistent page, since re-rolling at brief time re-reads every linked run before the decision rows are printed.
A refusal in the decision section, since the brief detects that the run behind a linked payoff has changed since linking.
The new run's mean in the decision section and the old one in the economics section, since only the tree is refreshed.
An NPV summary the tree never saw beside an Optimal EMV built on the older copied mean, with both provenance lines true.
explanation: Re-rolling recomputes the tree without refreshing what the tree copied, so the page disagrees with itself; linking the run again in the Decision Tree Builder brings the two sections back into line.

prompt: Writing up the EKPAN tree with its linked summary, an analyst labels the numbers. Which labelling follows the course's percentile convention?
options: NPV P90 185.0000 as the low case and NPV P10 710.0000 as the high case, with the 0.350000 success chance as a plain probability.
A high case for the NPV P90 of 185.0000, because a larger percentile number marks a larger outcome, and a plain success chance.
The low case for the NPV P90 of 185.0000, and the success chance written as a P35 so that readers can see it is uncertain.
NPV P10 710.0000 as the low case, since only 10 percent of the runs fall below it, with a plain success chance.
explanation: Under the exceedance meaning P90 is the low case, which is why the brief's economics rows read NPV P90 (low), NPV P50 and NPV P10 (high); a probability, likelihood or posterior never takes a P-label.

prompt: The EKPAN tree briefs with a Decision advantage of 67.2500. What does that number say?
options: That Drill beats Farm out by at least 67.2500 in every outcome, a margin of safety the farm-out cannot close in any case.
That the drill branch's mean exceeds the farm-out's by 67.2500; the drill still loses money with probability 0.500000.
That the drill's probability weighted gains exceed its probability weighted losses by 67.2500 once the farm-out is set aside.
That a survey on the EKPAN tree could add up to 67.2500 before the recommended first move would change to Farm out.
explanation: On the EKPAN tree it is 105.0000 less 37.7500, a difference of two means; after the 55.0000 drill cost the outcomes are 365.0000, 115.0000 and -80.0000, and 105.0000 is none of them.

prompt: A chance node named "Three equal outcomes" pays 30, 60 and 90, and each of its three branches is typed as 0.333333. What does the rollback engine return?
options: An emv of 60.0000, because a sum of 0.999999 sits exactly 1e-6 from 1 and the tolerance on a chance node is inclusive at its edge, so the node passes.
An emv of 60.0000, because the 1e-12 representation allowance added in the EC4-0 repair absorbs the binary residue on a probability sum as well as on an implied prior.
A refusal, `Chance branch probabilities sum to 0.999999, expected 1`, because three copies of 0.333333 land a hair more than 1e-6 from 1 in binary and the sum check carries no allowance for that.
An emv just under 60.0000, because the engine accepts the sum and weights the three payoffs by the thirds exactly as they were typed.
explanation: In binary the gap is 0.0000010000000000287557, just above 1e-6, so the node is refused while its message prints 0.999999; typed as 0.3333333 it rolls back to 60.0000. The 1e-12 allowance belongs to the implied-priors check alone, and whether to add one here is an open owner decision (finding EC4-8).

prompt: The published justInsideTolerance case states a success chance of 0.300000 and implies 0.305000. How does the repaired implied-priors check read it, and why?
options: Consistent true, because the delta, which is 0.0050000000000000044 in binary, is compared against 0.005 plus a 1e-12 representation allowance.
Consistent false, because in binary floating point the delta is 0.0050000000000000044, which is above the 0.005 threshold by 4.3e-18, so even an inclusive comparison turns it away.
Consistent true, because the engine rounds every delta to six decimals, 5.000000e-3, before comparing it with the threshold.
Consistent true, because the repair widened the threshold to 6.000000e-3 so that cases on the old boundary stop flipping.
explanation: Compared against 0.005 alone the case would read false, which is what the engine did before EC4-0 (finding D1, now resolved). The allowance absorbs a 4.3e-18 overshoot and nothing of a size worth arguing about.

prompt: A reviewer argues that since the EC4-0 repair added an allowance to the half percent check, an implied success chance of 0.306000 against a stated 0.3 ought to pass now. What does the Analyzer do with published withheldPastHalfPercent?
options: It prints a gross voi of 35.10, because the allowance moved the inclusive boundary far enough out to take in a delta just past half a percent.
It refuses the inputs with a message naming the sum in percent, because a delta above half a percent means the typed chances are not a distribution.
It prints every card with a consistency warning beside them, since the repair only annotates a value built on chances that disagree.
It withholds the value of information, because the allowance is 1e-12 and a delta of 6.000000e-3 is inconsistent before and after the repair.
explanation: The Analyzer still reports EMV without information 15.00 and EVPI 63.00. The gross voi of 35.10 it printed for these inputs before the repair is history, a number built on chances that cannot all be true.

prompt: One engine family holds two boundaries: a chance node's probabilities must sum to within 1e-6 of 1, and an implied chance must sit within 0.005 of the stated one. What happens exactly at each edge?
options: Both edges hold, because the EC4-0 repair gave each of the two comparisons the same 1e-12 allowance for binary representation error.
The implied-priors edge holds because of its 1e-12 allowance, while the sum edge has none, so thirds typed as 0.333333 are refused although their decimal gap equals the tolerance.
Both edges fail, because binary rounding pushes a value sitting exactly on either threshold a hair past it and neither check makes any allowance for that.
The sum edge holds because its message prints 0.999999, while the implied-priors edge fails at 0.305000 on 4.3e-18 of binary overshoot.
explanation: 0.305 less 0.3 evaluates to 0.0050000000000000044 and passes under the allowance; three copies of 0.333333 leave a gap of 0.0000010000000000287557 and are refused. Two boundaries in the same engine behave differently at their edge.

prompt: Branch A pays 20 with its cost typed as "abc", and branch B pays 12 at no cost. What does the rollback return?
options: A refusal naming branch A, because the engine checks that every cost reads as a number in the same way that it checks every payoff.
An emv of 20.0000 with A best and no message, because a cost that does not read as a number is charged as zero.
An emv of 15.0000 with A best, because text typed on a cost is converted to the number the user most likely meant, which here is 5.
An emv of 12.0000 with B best, because the engine drops a branch whose cost cannot be read and rolls back only what remains.
explanation: The intended reading at a cost of 5 is 15.0000, so the root is overstated by the whole cost while the first move still looks sensible. The check is arithmetic: a branch value equal to its child value means the cost was never charged.

prompt: On the decision where A pays 20 at a cost of 5 and B pays 12, three slips are made one at a time: A's cost typed as "abc", A's cost typed as -5, and A's payoff left empty. Which slip changes the recommendation?
options: The cost typed as "abc", because a branch carrying a cost the engine cannot read is valued at 0 and loses to B at 12.0000.
The cost typed as -5, because the engine refuses a negative cost on A and B becomes the only branch it is able to roll back.
None of the three, since each default leaves A ahead: 20.0000 for the text cost, 25.0000 for the receipt and 15.0000 for the empty payoff.
The empty payoff, which is read as 0, so branch A becomes -5.0000 and B wins at 12.0000.
explanation: A missing payoff is the more dangerous default: "abc" lifts A to 20.0000 and -5 lifts it to 25.0000, both still best, while an empty or null payoff flips the choice. A payoff of "20abc", by contrast, is refused with `Terminal payoff is not a number`.

prompt: Why is a cost typed as -5 on branch A, which pays 20, accepted and valued at 25.0000?
options: The engine reads a negative cost as money received, which is right for a farm-in carry and a typing error for everything else, and it cannot tell the two apart.
The engine flags the negative cost as a receipt in its output, so the 25.0000 arrives with a note that a reviewer is expected to read before using it.
The engine charges an unreadable cost as zero and then adds the typed magnitude back as a separate receipt on the same branch.
A branch value is the child value plus its cost, so any cost typed on A adds to it and a cost of 5 would give the same 25.0000.
explanation: A branch value is the child value less the cost, so 20 less -5 is 25.0000, and nothing in the output marks it; a cost of 5 gives 15.0000. Only a reader who checks each branch value against the cost they meant will see it.

prompt: In the Decision Tree Builder a user clears the probability box on the branch paying 10 of a two-branch chance node paying 10 and 30, and the branch paying 30 already reads 1. What happens?
options: The cleared box stores 0, the sum falls short of 1, and the node is refused with a message that prints the sum to six decimals.
The cleared box keeps its last saved value until a new number is typed, so the node rolls back exactly as it did before the edit and the drawing keeps the old chance.
The cleared box stores 0, the sum is still 1 so the check passes, and the node returns 30.0000 with the cleared branch gone from the weighting.
The node returns 20.0000, because an empty probability is shared out equally with the other branch before the payoffs are weighted.
explanation: A cleared probability usually surfaces as a sum that is not 1 and is refused; it passes only when the other branches already sum to 1. The engine gives the same 30.0000 for a probability typed as an empty string beside a 1, and 20.0000 comes from typing one probability as the text "0.5" beside 0.5.

prompt: The published refusal case puts a bad distribution at node "cc", two levels under the root, whose probabilities sum to 0.200000. What does the rollback return for the rest of the tree?
options: The root EMV with the faulty chance node valued at zero, and a message beside it naming "cc" as the node that was skipped over.
The root EMV with node "cc" rescaled to sum to 1, since 0.200000 is a proportion the engine can normalise.
Values for every branch that does not pass through "cc", with the best branch chosen from among those that could be rolled back.
Nothing: the message names node "cc", and there is no root EMV, no best branch and no value for the healthy branches.
explanation: `Chance branch probabilities sum to 0.200000, expected 1 (at node "cc")` is the whole answer. One bad node stops the tree, so the node label in the message is the only pointer to where the fault lives.

prompt: The Bayes calculation behind EVII checks the likelihoods of the EKPAN lottery's survey before it computes anything. Which numbers must sum to 1?
options: Each signal's likelihoods across the outcomes, so a bright spot's 0.850000 given Success and 0.250000 given a dry hole must together sum to 1.
Each outcome's likelihoods down its column across the signals, so the Success column reads 0.850000 for a bright spot and 0.150000 for none.
The chances of the signals themselves, 0.460000 for a bright spot and 0.540000 for none, which the engine checks before any posterior.
The posteriors after each signal, 0.646739 and 0.353261 after a bright spot, since those are the numbers the action is chosen on.
explanation: The survey passes because Success reads 0.850000 / 0.150000 and Dry hole 0.250000 / 0.750000. A Dry hole column summing to 1.200000 is refused with the outcome named; the signal chances and posteriors are derived, never typed.

prompt: The EKPAN lottery is typed into the repaired VOI Analyzer with Bright spot at 46.000000 percent and No bright spot at 64 percent. What does the Analyzer show?
options: No cards at all, only the refusal `Indicator chances sum to 110 percent, expected 100`.
EMV without information 75.75 and EVPI 52.00, with the value of information withheld because the indicators contradict the stated prior.
A refusal stating the indicator sum as a fraction of 1 rather than in percent, the engine's internal scale for every chance it checks.
The cards for renormalised indicator chances, since the Analyzer rescales any indicator set that misses 100 before valuing the survey.
explanation: Indicator chances that are not a distribution are refused before anything is computed, with the sum in percent. Withholding with 75.75 and 52.00 is the answer for chances that do sum to 100 but contradict the stated outcome chances.

prompt: IRRI types both indicators as 20 / 80 percent, and published indicatorChancesAboveHundred types indicator chances summing to 110 percent. How do the repaired Analyzer's answers differ?
options: Both are refused with a message naming the sum in percent, because each set of typed percents fails the check before any card is drawn.
Both are withheld with 15.00 and 63.00 reported, because each describes chances that the stated outcome chances cannot support.
IRRI is withheld and still reports EMV without information 15.00 and EVPI 63.00, while the 110 percent case is refused and shows no card.
IRRI is refused because its implied success chance of 0.200000 is not the stated 0.3, while the 110 percent case is withheld with two cards.
explanation: A refusal says the numbers are not chances at all; a withholding says they are chances that cannot all be true together. EMV without information and EVPI depend only on the stated outcome chances, so 15.00 and 63.00 survive a withholding.

prompt: Before the EC4-0 repair, which input the Analyzer now refuses printed a gross voi that looked exactly like a genuine answer on its default study?
options: posteriorsAboveHundred, whose 69.00 sat close enough to the evpi card of 63.00 that nothing on the screen marked it out as a problem.
chanceOutsideRange, whose -15.00 read as an ordinary survey priced above its worth rather than as a gross value below the floor of zero.
indicatorChancesAboveHundred, whose 33.00 is the default study's own voi, printed for indicator chances summing to 110 percent.
missingOutcomeChanceCountsAsZero, whose 41.00 is the default study's own EMV with information, so it looked familiar to anyone who ran the defaults.
explanation: These cards are history, reconstructed from engine calls. 69.00 is above the 63.00 ceiling and -15.00 is below zero, both impossible on sight; 33.00 is the default study's genuine voi and could not be caught by eye, while its EMV with information is 38.00.

prompt: Published posteriorsOffsetButPriorsAgree types outcome chances given Positive Seismic that sum to 110 percent, built so that the priors they imply equal the stated ones. Why does a reviewer who checks only the implied priors miss it?
options: The implied-priors test passes, and only the check that each set of outcome chances sums to 100 catches it, which the Analyzer runs first and refuses on.
The implied-priors test is run on rounded posteriors, so an offset of 10 percent is absorbed inside the half percent tolerance before it can register at all.
The reviewer's test is the right one, and the Analyzer passes the case too, since priors that agree prove every typed number is a chance.
The implied-priors test fails on this case, but the Analyzer reports that failure as a withholding, so the reviewer takes the missing cards for a refusal.
explanation: The refusal reads `Outcome chances given "Positive Seismic" sum to 110 percent, expected 100`. Before the repair the same inputs printed a gross voi of 42.50 beside an evpi card of 63.00, a plausible number built on percents that were not chances.

prompt: Thirds typed as 0.333 on "Three equal outcomes", paying 30, 60 and 90, are refused. A user repairs the node by nudging the branch paying 90 until the sum reads 1. What is wrong with that repair?
options: Nothing, because the tolerance of 1e-6 exists precisely so a user can close a rounding gap on whichever branch is most convenient to edit by hand.
It is refused again, because the engine compares each branch with the others and requires equal chances on a node whose payoffs are evenly spaced.
It moves the EMV only in the sixth decimal, which the rollback does not print at four places, so the result still reads 60.0000.
The node passes but no longer says the outcomes are equally likely, so the EMV moves off 60.0000 by whatever the nudge put on that branch.
explanation: The repair is to type every third to seven places: 0.3333333 on each branch sums to 1.000000 and rolls back to 60.0000. A nudge changes the chances unequally, which is a different tree that happens to pass the check.

prompt: On the EKPAN lottery at a success probability of 0.35 the drill is worth 75.7500 and the farm-out 33.2500. What would make either decision module recommend the farm-out at these same payoffs and chances?
options: Setting a risk tolerance below the drill's loss of 80.0000, which the rollback reads before comparing the two means.
Nothing in either module, since both maximise expected money and neither holds a utility function or a risk aversion setting.
The drill's 0.650000 chance of losing money, since the engine demotes an action that loses more often than it wins.
A higher discount rate on the drill's success payoff, because the rollback applies the rate typed on each terminal before weighting.
explanation: The engine sees only the two means: 0.350000 x 365.0000 plus 0.650000 x -80.0000 is 75.7500. A preference for the farm-out belongs in words beside the tree, never hidden in a payoff quietly lowered until the farm-out wins.

prompt: The EKPAN lottery's survey has an EVII of 24.8250. With the survey the drill is chosen only after a bright spot, so the joint chance of drilling a dry hole falls from 0.650000 to 0.162500. How much of that fall is priced in the 24.8250?
options: All of it, because the posterior after a bright spot is built from the dry-hole joint chance and so carries the reduction in risk inside it.
The part that falls on the no bright spot reading, since the farm-out chosen there with probability 0.540000 never loses on the well.
Most of it, since EVII is the EVPI of 52.0000 scaled down by how far the survey cuts the chance of drilling a dry hole.
None of it, because EVII is a difference of means and prices only the rise in expected money.
explanation: A risk averse buyer would pay more than 24.8250 for this survey, and the engine cannot say how much more. The 0.162500 is a joint chance; the posterior of a dry hole after a bright spot is 0.353261.

prompt: A small tree values Drill at 40.0000 less a cost of 10.0000 and Farm out at 30.0000. Listed Drill first it recommends Drill; listed Farm out first it recommends Farm out. What decides the recommendation?
options: The listing order, because a decision node replaces its incumbent only on a strictly greater value, so the first of two equal branches is kept.
Floating-point residue in the cost subtraction, which leaves one of the branches a few binary digits ahead depending on which is evaluated first.
The branch with the lower cost, since the engine breaks an equal EMV in favour of the action that commits less money up front.
The last branch evaluated, because a decision node overwrites its best choice whenever a later value is at least as large.
explanation: Both orderings return an emv of 30.0000, and only the label follows the order in which somebody typed the branches. Residue decides at a computed switch point such as 0.228571 on the EKPAN lottery; 40.0000 less 10.0000 is exactly 30.0000.

prompt: In the VOI Analyzer, Success at 25 percent pays 200, Dry hole at 75 percent pays -50, and the decision cost is 12.5. The insight names 'Drill Exploration Well' as the optimal decision beside an EMV without information of 0.00. Why that action?
options: Acting is worth a small binary residue above 0 once the cost is subtracted, and the Analyzer names whichever action leads by that residue.
The Analyzer names the risky action whenever the net value is positive, and the netVoi card reads 20.00.
Acting is worth exactly 0, the same as "Do Not", and the named decision is listed first, so it keeps an exact tie.
The Analyzer compares its actions before charging the decision cost of 12.5, so drilling leads by that amount before any card is filled.
explanation: 0.25 x 200 plus 0.75 x -50 less 12.5 is exactly 0, and nothing on the screen says walking away is worth the same. The gross voi of 25.00 is large precisely because the prior decision is perfectly unsettled.

prompt: A Decision Studio brief for published equalEmvTie prints Optimal EMV 30.0000 and Recommended first move "A". Which row shows that the recommendation is a tie?
options: Decision advantage, which reads 0.0000 because Next best alternative is also 30.0000.
Recommended first move, which appends the tied branch "B" after "A" whenever two root branches share the optimal value.
Next best alternative, which reads 29.9990 for "C" and so shows that the runner-up sits only a hair below the choice.
Optimal EMV, which is printed without decimals when two branches tie so that a reader can see the value is shared.
explanation: Next best alternative is the largest other root branch value, "B" at 30.0000, while "C" is 29.9990. The advantage row is the only place the tie is visible, so read it before the first move.

prompt: On the Analyzer's default study the gross voi is 33.00. At a survey cost of 32.996 the netVoi card reads 0.00. What does the verdict sentence say?
options: The information exactly pays for itself, because the verdict reads the two-decimal card and the card says 0.00.
Since this is positive, acquiring the information is financially advantageous, because the verdict tests the net value before it is rounded.
No verdict at all, since the Analyzer drops the sentence whenever a card rounds to zero and leaves the choice to the reader.
The information exactly pays for itself, because a net value within half a cent of zero falls inside the Analyzer's neutral band.
explanation: 33 less 32.996 is a small positive amount: the card rounds it to 0.00 and the sentence tests its sign. Only at a cost of exactly 33.000 do the card and the sentence both say neutral; no neutral band exists.

prompt: Priced at 33.004, the default survey shows -0.00 on its net value card. What is the sign telling a reader?
options: Nothing, since -0.00 and 0.00 are the same number on a two-decimal card and the verdict beside both of them reads value-neutral.
That the survey cost was entered as a negative receipt, which the Analyzer marks with a sign on an otherwise zero card.
That the consistency check found a small disagreement, which the Analyzer reports as a signed zero in place of withholding.
That the net value before rounding is a small negative amount whose sign the rounding kept, which is why the verdict says the survey is not justified.
explanation: The cards are toFixed(2) strings: 33 less 33.004 is negative and prints -0.00, and the verdict reads that same value unrounded and writes negative. At 32.996 the card reads 0.00 beside a positive verdict.

prompt: A netVoi card reads 0.00 and the verdict beside it says positive. What does a careful reader report?
options: That the survey is a positive investment, because the verdict tests the unrounded number and is therefore the more precise of the two readings.
That the survey is value-neutral, because the card is what the Analyzer displays and a sentence can never be more precise than its card.
That the survey is priced at its value, found by comparing the cost with the gross voi, since the cost that makes information neutral is the gross value, 33.00 on the default study.
That the survey is worth buying at any cost below the evpi card of 63.00, since the ceiling bounds the price and the gross value only bounds the net.
explanation: Costs of 32.996 and 33.004 are indistinguishable in any real tender, so a verdict flipping between them reports the sign of a residue. On the EKPAN lottery's full survey the neutral price is its gross 24.8250.

prompt: A symmetric survey on the EKPAN lottery at accuracy 0.600000 moves the success chance after a "reads dry" result from 0.35 to 0.264151. Why is its EVII 0.0000?
options: Because an accuracy of 0.600000 is too close to a coin toss for the engine to run Bayes, so it reports the prior's value in place of a posterior.
Because 0.264151 is still above the drill against farm-out switch of 0.228571, so both readings lead to Drill and no action changes.
Because the success chance after "reads success", 0.446809, rises by more than the other reading falls, and the two changes cancel in value.
Because EVII is floored at zero, and the small negative value this survey really has is clamped to 0.0000 for display.
explanation: Weighting Drill's value at each posterior by the chance of each reading returns Drill's value at the prior, 75.7500. Beliefs moved and no decision did; the survey first changes an action at accuracy 0.645051.

prompt: The same symmetric survey on the EKPAN lottery is worth 0.7250 at accuracy 0.650000. What changed from accuracy 0.600000?
options: A "reads dry" result now moves the success chance to 0.224771, below the switch of 0.228571, so that reading leads to the farm-out.
A "reads success" result now moves the success chance to 0.500000, which makes Drill worth more after that reading than at the prior.
The survey became more accurate than the prior of 0.35, and information is worth something once its accuracy beats the prior chance.
The EVPI of 52.0000 began to pass through to the survey, which receives a share of it in proportion to its accuracy above one half.
explanation: The survey first changes an action at 0.645051, and just past it that single changed reading adds 0.7250. After "reads success" the action was already Drill, so a larger shift there adds nothing.

prompt: At accuracy 0.550000 the engine returns an EVII of -1.42e-14 for the symmetric survey on the EKPAN lottery. How should that be read?
options: As a small genuine loss, because a survey this weak misleads often enough to cost a sliver of expected money whenever it is bought.
As the mark of inputs that contradict each other, which the Bayes engine reports as a negative value where the Analyzer would withhold one.
As the tie rule at work, because both readings lead to Drill and the engine subtracts the branch listed second from the branch listed first.
As 0.0000, floating-point residue from subtracting two equal sums, printed as zero below 1e-9.
explanation: Information derived by Bayes can never be worth less than 0, and the Bayes engine derives its posteriors from likelihoods, so its inputs cannot contradict each other. Both readings lead to Drill, so the value is 0.0000.

prompt: The published dominantAction lottery has Always paying 100.0000 / 50.0000 and Never paying 10.0000 / 5.0000, with an evpi of 0.0000. Why is perfect information worthless there?
options: The outcome is already certain, so nothing is left to learn and the value with perfect information matches the value at the prior.
The signal's readings do not depend on the outcome, so every posterior stays at the prior and no action is ever able to move.
Never loses nothing in either outcome, so a decision maker can always fall back on it and information has no downside left to remove.
Always is best in both outcomes, so knowing the outcome never changes the action, and evWithPerfect equals emvPrior at 65.0000.
explanation: Perfect information takes the best action per outcome, and that is Always both times. The certainOutcome lottery reaches 0.0000 another way, with emvPrior and evWithPerfect both 260.0000, and uselessSignal is an EVII of 0.0000.

prompt: Published threeByThree has three readings and costs 12.0000; after "Dim" it recommends the farm-out, worth 15.3333. Why is its evii only 1.2000 against an evpi of 24.0000?
options: Its three readings split the 24.0000 of perfect information between them, and the "Dim" reading carries the smallest share of it.
Its evii is reported net of the survey cost, so 1.2000 is what is left once most of the 12.0000 price is paid.
It changes one action, on one reading, and is worth only what that single change adds, so its netEvii at 12.0000 is -10.8000.
One of its readings is too unlikely to carry a posterior and is dropped, so only two readings contribute value.
explanation: Bright and Flat both still lead to Drill alone, so the survey adds nothing on those readings. Its gross 1.2000 is a tenth of the 12.0000 price, and the information tree chooses No further information.

prompt: The EKPAN tree's success payoff is linked in the Decision Tree Builder to a Monte Carlo summary with mean 420, P90 185, P50 390 and P10 710 (P90 the low case), and the run is revalued afterwards. What does the tree show?
options: 105.0000 from the mean copied at the moment of linking, because only the mean enters and nothing re-reads the run until it is linked again.
The revalued run's mean, because the Builder re-reads a linked run every time the tree is rolled back so that the payoff stays current.
A value between its P90 and P10 cases, because the rollback weights the three percentiles of a linked summary ahead of the chance node.
37.7500 with the farm-out recommended, because a linked summary enters at its P90, the conservative case for an exploration payoff.
explanation: A linked summary is a copy taken at link time. Read at its P90 of 185 the EKPAN tree would fall to 37.7500 and flip to the farm-out; at the mean it is identical to a plain 420.0000 payoff, and the spread is carried and never used.

prompt: The EKPAN lottery's survey typed into the VOI Analyzer gives a gross voi of 19.84, while the Bayes engine values the same survey at 24.8250. Which is correct?
options: 24.8250 only, since the Analyzer rounds the posteriors it is given to whole percents and loses the difference in that rounding before valuing them.
Both: 19.84 is the value when the only actions are the drill and "Do Not", and 24.8250 is the value with the farm-out available.
19.84 only, because the Bayes engine values the survey before the drill cost of 55.0000 is charged and so overstates it.
Neither, because a survey that changes the action after only one of its readings must be valued at its EVPI of 52.0000.
explanation: The Analyzer offers exactly two actions; with Farm out removed the Bayes engine gives an evii of 19.8375, which is the 19.84. The Analyzer values one survey before one decision and has no place for a third action.

prompt: IRRI types both of the Analyzer's indicators as 20 / 80 percent against stated outcome chances of 30 / 70. What does an expert reading write down?
options: A value of information of -15.00, worked out by hand from the typed chances, since the repaired Analyzer no longer prints one.
A value of information of 0.00, since a withheld value means the survey cannot change the decision and so is worth nothing.
No numbers at all, because indicator chances that contradict the stated ones are refused before the Analyzer computes anything.
EMV without information 15.00 and EVPI 63.00, with the value of information withheld because the inputs imply a success chance of 0.200000.
explanation: The two surviving cards depend only on the stated outcome chances. -15.00 is the gross voi printed before the EC4-0 repair, history and below the zero floor that Bayes guarantees, and a withheld value is never written as 0.00.

prompt: Before the EC4-0 repair, published certainPosteriorsWithheld printed a gross voi of 245.00. What made that number impossible on sight?
options: It sat below the default study's genuine gross voi of 33.00, which any survey on those same payoffs must at least reach.
It sat above the evpi card of 63.00, and no information can be worth more than perfect information.
It turned negative once the survey cost of 10.0000 was taken off, and a net value below zero cannot come out of Bayes.
Its implied success chance of 1.000000 lies outside the range the Analyzer accepts, so the value rested on an out-of-range input.
explanation: The inputs imply 1.000000 / 0.000000 against a stated 0.300000 / 0.700000, and the net value then was 235.00. The repaired Analyzer reports 15.00 and 63.00 and withholds the rest.

prompt: The EKPAN lottery's survey is typed into the Analyzer with its posteriors rounded to 65 and 10 percent, which passes with a gross voi of 20.51. What happens when they are rounded to 65 and 8 percent?
options: It passes with a gross voi of 20.51 as well, because rounding a posterior to a whole percent never moves the implied prior by half a percent.
It is refused, because posteriors rounded to whole percents no longer sum to 100 under each indicator and so are not chances.
The value of information is withheld, because the implied success chance is 0.342200, a delta of -7.800000e-3, outside the 0.005 check.
It passes with a gross voi of 19.84, because the Analyzer recovers full-precision posteriors from the indicator chances before valuing.
explanation: At 65 and 10 the implied chance is 0.353000, within 0.005 of the stated 0.35; at 65 and 8 it is 0.342200 and the Analyzer withholds. 19.84 is the gross voi at full precision.

prompt: The first step of an expert case adds every set of typed percents. The EKPAN lottery typed with No bright spot at 64 percent fails it. What is the answer for that case?
options: The refusal message, `Indicator chances sum to 110 percent, expected 100`, and the box at fault, since a refused case has no value.
EMV without information 75.75 and EVPI 52.00 with the value of information withheld, as for any typed inputs that fail a check.
The values from the later steps with No bright spot corrected so that the pair sums to 100, since the message names the box that was mistyped.
The gross voi the Analyzer printed before the repair, since a refused case is valued the way the Analyzer valued it before EC4-0.
explanation: The indicator chances sum to 110.000000 percent, so they are not a distribution. Withholding with 75.75 and 52.00 answers chances that sum correctly but contradict each other, and the message never says whether 64 or 46.000000 is the slip.

prompt: In the second step an expert rebuilds the EKPAN lottery's implied prior by hand from its survey. Which arithmetic is right?
options: 0.850000 plus 0.150000 gives 1 down the Success column, so the stated prior of 0.350000 holds by construction.
0.646739 and 0.097222 averaged equally over the two readings give the stated prior of 0.350000 to within the 0.005 check.
0.297500 plus 0.162500 gives 0.460000, and that joint total is the implied prior the stated 0.350000 is compared against.
explanation: The implied chance of an outcome is the sum over the indicators of each indicator's chance times the outcome's chance given it. 0.297500 plus 0.162500 is the chance of a bright spot, and the likelihood columns are a separate check.

prompt: An expert case lists a three-outcome lottery with Drill alone at 109.0000, Drill with partner at 54.5000, Farm out at 31.0000 and Relinquish at 0.0000. Why can Drill with partner never be the best action at any probability?
options: It falls below Farm out once the Large chance drops under 0.200000, and above that chance Drill alone overtakes it, so no window is left.
Its partner's share is charged as a cost after weighting, which pulls the value below Relinquish whenever the Dry chance exceeds 0.300000.
It becomes best only at a Large chance of 0.500000, which the sweep never counts because the Dry chance would then be 0.000000.
It is exactly half of Drill alone everywhere: half of a positive value is smaller, and half of a negative one is still negative while Farm out never falls below 0.
explanation: The sweep holding Medium at 0.5 has one switch, between Farm out and Drill alone; at a Large chance of 0.000000 Drill with partner is 2.5000 against Farm out at 15.0000. The third step still lists it, valued.

prompt: In the fourth step, perfect information on the EKPAN lottery needs the best action after a dry hole, where Farm out and Walk away both pay 0.0000. Does that tie change the EVPI?
options: Yes: the tie goes to Farm out as the branch listed first, and its 95.0000 on a success lifts the expected value with perfect information.
No: EVPI takes the best value per outcome, so 0.350000 x 365.0000 gives 127.7500 and, less 75.7500, the EVPI is 52.0000 whichever is named.
Yes: at a tie the engine averages the two tied actions, which halves the contribution of the dry hole to the value with perfect information.
No, but only because Walk away is dropped from a lottery where the farm-out pays at least as much in every outcome, so no tie exists.
explanation: Both tied actions pay 0.0000 on a dry hole, so 0.650000 x 0.0000 adds nothing whichever is named. A tie changes a label and never the value taken.

prompt: On the EKPAN lottery an expert values the survey at a cost of 8.0000. Which set of figures belongs in the report?
options: Gross 24.8250, net 16.8250, a neutral price equal to the gross 24.8250, and bounds of 0 and 52.0000 on the gross.
Gross 24.8250, net 16.8250, and a neutral price of 52.0000, since information stays worth buying until its cost reaches the EVPI ceiling.
Gross 16.8250 and net 8.8250, since the survey cost is taken off once inside the information tree and again when the net is reported.
Gross 100.5750 and net 92.5750, since the value of information is the expected value with the survey before the prior is subtracted.
explanation: EVII is 100.5750 less 75.7500. The information tree's two root branches tie at a survey cost of 24.8250, where the engine keeps the acquisition as the branch listed first.

prompt: A case asks what the EKPAN lottery's survey is worth with all three of its actions available, and a candidate writes the Analyzer's gross voi of 19.84. What went wrong?
options: The right number for the wrong question: 19.84 is the two-action value, and with the farm-out available the survey is worth 24.8250.
Nothing, because the Analyzer is the published tool for this question and its 19.84 supersedes a hand calculation on the Bayes engine.
A rounding slip, since 19.84 is the Bayes engine's 24.8250 after the posteriors are rounded to whole percents inside the Analyzer.
The candidate quoted the net value, since 19.84 is what remains after the survey cost and the gross value sits in the guidance sentence.
explanation: The Analyzer offers only the named decision and "Do Not"; the Bayes engine without the farm-out gives 19.8375. The Analyzer's netVoi card for the same survey reads 11.84 and its evpi card 52.00.

prompt: The onward lesson takes decision analysis on to capital portfolio decisions under one budget. Why is the best set of projects not simply the set of individually best ones?
options: Because each project's EMV has to be turned into a net value of information before projects on different prospects can be compared at all.
Because a portfolio rolls every project back at the discount rate of its riskiest member, which lowers each value unevenly and so reorders them.
Because money spent on one project is unavailable to the next, so each is judged against what else the same budget buys.
Because an individually best project was valued with its own information already bought, and a portfolio has to strip every survey value out first.
explanation: Capital portfolio decisions choose among many projects under one budget, and money spent on one is unavailable to the next, so the choice is of a set under that constraint. Decision Studio already sets capital allocation from a saved portfolio beside the decision analysis in one brief.

prompt: A Decision Studio brief for the EKPAN tree prints Optimal EMV 105.0000, Next best alternative 37.7500 and Decision advantage 67.2500, with the success payoff linked to a Monte Carlo summary. Read at the summary's P90 of 185.0000, the low case, what would change?
options: Nothing, because the brief re-reads the linked run at brief time and the run's mean has not moved since it was saved.
The advantage would shrink by the gap between the mean and the P90, while Drill stayed the recommended first move.
The tree would rise to 206.5000, because the P90 of a Monte Carlo summary is its high case under the exceedance convention.
The tree would fall to 37.7500 and the choice would flip to the farm-out, though the brief rightly uses the mean, the only statistic a linear rollback needs.
explanation: With success at 185.0000 the drill branch is worth 22.7500 against the farm-out's 37.7500. At the mean of 420 the brief's 105.0000 is identical to a plain payoff, and 206.5000 belongs to the P10, the high case.

prompt: OKRIKA appraises at 87.0000 against selling now at 48.0000. Without the option to sell after a poor appraisal, the appraisal branch would be worth 15.6000. What does the difference between 87.0000 and 15.6000 price?
options: The appraisal's information, since 71.4000 is what appraising adds over developing now at 33.6000.
The later choice: the option to sell after a poor result is worth 71.4000 inside the appraisal branch.
The decision advantage, since 71.4000 is how far the recommended first move leads the next best alternative in the brief.
The first move itself, since 71.4000 is what the root would lose if Sell now at 48.0000 were struck from the tree.
explanation: 87.0000 less 15.6000 is 71.4000. Without the later choice the root would sell now at 48.0000, and with it the brief's Decision advantage for Appraise is 39.0000.

prompt: The story so far says thirds typed as 0.333 are refused while 0.3333333 rolls back to 60.0000. Where do thirds typed to six places, 0.333333, fall?
options: Accepted at 60.0000, because the message would print 0.999999, which is exactly 1e-6 short and inside a tolerance that includes its edge.
Accepted at 60.0000, because the EC4-0 repair gave the chance node sum the same 1e-12 allowance that holds the half percent boundary.
Accepted just below 60.0000, because the engine weights the payoffs by 0.333333 each and reports the slightly smaller mean.
Refused, because in binary their sum misses 1 by 0.0000010000000000287557 and the chance node check makes no allowance for binary rounding.
explanation: Six places and fewer are refused and seven land inside 1e-6. The 1e-12 allowance belongs to the implied-priors check alone; adding one here is an open owner decision (finding EC4-8).

prompt: The half percent boundary on implied priors holds in the repaired check. What holds it?
options: A 1e-12 allowance on top of 0.005, which absorbs 0.0050000000000000044, the binary value of 0.305 less 0.3.
An inclusive comparison against 0.005 alone, which suffices because 0.305 less 0.3 is exactly 0.005 in binary floating point.
A threshold widened to 6.000000e-3, which is why an implied chance of 0.306000 is the first case the Analyzer withholds.
Rounding each implied chance to six decimals before the delta is taken, so that 0.305000 less 0.300000 comes out exact.
explanation: The binary delta overshoots 0.005 by 4.3e-18, and before EC4-0 the engine had no allowance and called justInsideTolerance inconsistent (finding D1). An implied 0.306000 is inconsistent before and after the repair.

prompt: An expert writes one sentence reporting the EKPAN lottery's survey. Which sentence carries everything the reading asks for?
options: Worth 19.84 gross in the Analyzer and 11.84 net, which is its value because the Analyzer is the published tool for this very question.
Worth 24.8250 gross and worth buying at any cost up to its ceiling of 52.0000, since the EVPI is the price that makes information neutral.
Worth 24.8250 gross and 16.8250 net at a cost of 8.0000, against a ceiling of 52.0000, with drill, farm-out and walk away as the actions.
Worth 16.8250 as the value of the survey, since the cost of 8.0000 is already inside the information tree and needs no separate mention.
explanation: A value of information without its actions, its tree and its consistency is not a number: the same survey is 19.84 in the two-action Analyzer. The price that makes the survey neutral is the gross 24.8250, below the 52.0000 ceiling.

prompt: A board says it cannot survive a loss of 80.0000 million USD on one well, and the EKPAN tree still recommends the drill at 105.0000. Why does the board's position change nothing in the rollback?
options: The loss is already priced in, because the EKPAN tree's dry hole of -25.0000 was discounted at a risk premium before it was typed into its terminal.
The limit bears on the farm-out as well, so it lowers both branch values together and leaves their order at the root unchanged.
The engine is risk neutral: it maximises expected money and has no utility function or risk aversion setting where that limit could be entered.
The EKPAN tree's drill cost of 55.0000 is charged before weighting, which caps the loss the rollback can see at the cost rather than at the whole dry hole outcome.
explanation: On the EKPAN tree the drill loses money with probability 0.500000 and still wins, 105.0000 against 37.7500, because the rollback ranks branches by their averages alone.

prompt: A tree arrives with one of its nodes typed "lottery" and every probability inside the range 0 to 1. What does the engine return?
options: A refusal naming an unknown node type at that node, and no EMV for any part of the tree.
An ordinary rollback that treats the node as a chance node, since a lottery is a set of weighted outcomes and its probabilities already sum to 1.
A rollback of the valid remainder, with the unrecognised node entered in its parent as a terminal worth 0.0000 until it is retyped.
The EMV of every level above the node, stopping where the tree stops being well formed and reporting the deepest valid value as the root.
explanation: The engine knows decision, chance and terminal nodes only and never guesses what a malformed node meant; as the published sum of 0.200000 two levels down shows, a refusal anywhere returns nothing.

prompt: An analyst discounts the EKPAN tree's payoffs by hand, although another engine had already discounted them, and leaves the drill cost of 55.0000 as typed. What does the rollback report?
options: A refusal, because the engine compares each payoff against the rate stored with its linked run and detects the second discount.
The same 105.0000 for the EKPAN tree, since the rollback restates every payoff to the date of the root decision before it weights them.
A larger EMV, because a smaller dry hole loss lifts the drill's weighted value by more than the shrunken success payoff takes away.
A smaller EMV with no warning, pulled toward the branch that carries less cost, because every payoff shrank while the cost stayed at face value.
explanation: The engine has no rate, no date and no field for either, so 420.0000 and -25.0000 enter the drill chance node exactly as typed and a second discount leaves no trace.

prompt: A tree passes every check the engine makes: known node types, at least one branch per node, and probabilities summing to 1 within 1e-6. What has that established?
options: That the recommended branch is robust, since a choice that turned inside the tolerance of 1e-6 would have been refused as ambiguous.
Only that the tree is well formed; nothing about whether its payoffs are discounted, its probabilities true, or its branches complete.
That no better branch was left off, since a decision node refuses to roll back when a walk-away at 0.0000 would beat every branch it was given.
That the chance nodes agree across stages, because the engine checks every later chance node against the ones above it.
explanation: The published allNegative case passes every check and recommends a branch worth -52.0000, because no walk-away was drawn and the engine never adds one.

prompt: A Builder terminal was linked to a saved Monte Carlo run with an NPV mean of 420, and the run has since been revalued. What does the tree roll back with?
options: The revalued mean, because the Builder re-reads every linked run each time a rollback is requested from the explorer.
The mean copied when the terminal was linked, until someone links it again.
The revalued P90, the low case, because a linked terminal falls back to that end of its summary whenever the run behind it has changed.
Nothing at all, because a stale link is refused with the message that the distribution payoff has no finite mean.
explanation: Linking stores a copy of the run's mean, P90 and P10 at that moment and nothing re-reads the run, so the EKPAN tree stays at 105.0000 whatever the run now holds.

prompt: Inside the EKPAN tree's drill chance node the Marginal outcome carries 170.0000, although the develop payoff below it is 260.0000. Where does 170.0000 come from?
options: The chance node averages the marginal find's Develop and Sell branches, because the later decision has not yet been made when the drill outcome is weighted.
The EKPAN tree's develop cost of 90.0000 is charged at the drill chance node after weighting, and 170.0000 is the figure the node shows once that charge is made.
